acceptance.bandBar: Signed up to {accept}% risk, held between {accept}% and {reject}%, declined from {reject}%
acceptance.deviceNote: Requests are decided while the app is running, in front or in the background. Nothing can sign in your name once it is closed.
acceptance.intro: Every purchase you sell into needs your signature. The app scores the buyer from the ledger — what the community backs them for, what they already owe, and how fast they are taking on debt — and signs the safe ones, declines the bad ones, and keeps the middle for you.
acceptance.maxAmountNote: The score prices the buyer, not the size of what you are granting. Leave it at 0 and every request waits for you.
acceptance.personalK: How much backing you want to see
acceptance.personalKNote: Move it right to want more backing behind somebody before the app calls them safe, left to want less. Leave it where it starts and you are using the community’s number.
acceptance.scopeNote: A request the ledger would reject is never signed. Key recoveries, guardian changes, arbitration and governance always wait for you, whatever they score.
acceptance.title: Acceptance rule
acceptance.deviceSummary: The rule and the signing key live on this device.
acceptance.maxAmountSummary: Anything above this waits for you, however well they score.
acceptance.personalKSummary: Your own reading of the community's one scale.
acceptance.scopeSummary: Only purchases where you grant credit are decided this way.
acceptance.summary: Set the rule once instead of judging every purchase.
acceptance.backgroundLabel: Keep deciding while the app is in the background
acceptance.backgroundSummary: The rule works while the app is behind something else, not once it is closed.
acceptance.backgroundNote: The rule signs on this device, so it decides for as long as this app is running. With this on, closing the window hides it instead, and a phone keeps a notice in your shade while edet works. Keep the phone on charge, or exempt edet from battery optimisation: a device left unplugged and still, with the screen off, has its network suspended by the system.
acceptance.backgroundUnavailable: This device could not keep the rule running in the background.
acceptance.batteryTitle: One setting is Android’s, not ours
acceptance.batteryBody: Android suspends an app’s network when the phone is left unplugged and still with the screen off, and edet cannot exempt itself. On the next screen, allow edet to run in the background — set its battery use to unrestricted. Keeping the phone on charge does the same thing.

background.serviceBody: Deciding requests in the background. Nothing signs once the app is closed.
background.lockedBody: Your acceptance rule is paused: open edet and enter your passphrase.
background.channelPaymentsDesc: A purchase your acceptance rule signed while you were not looking.
background.channelWaitingDesc: A request or an approval that only you can decide.

addressInput.byKey: Named by this key. It must be a member's, and they sign from their own app.
addressInput.excluded: That address cannot be the counterparty here.
addressInput.invalid: Not an address (0x + 40 hex) or public key (64 hex).
addressInput.newcomer: Nobody on this ledger holds that key yet — recording this trade is what creates their account. They sign it from their own app.
addressInput.unknown: No member with this address on your ledger.

browsing.note: You are looking around. Trading needs an identity on this device.

app.name: edet
app.vaultError: The identity vault on this device could not be opened. Your seeds are intact but unreadable (corrupt browser storage?). Restore from your recovery phrase or an exported backup on a fresh profile.

bond.alwaysFree: Always free. This action never sets aside any of your capacity — settling, curing and leaving never can.
bond.covered: Free — covered by your activity allowance ({left} of {total} left this epoch).
bond.reserves: Sets aside {amount} of your capacity for {epochs} epoch(s), then it comes back to you. Nothing is charged and nobody receives it.
bond.short: This would set aside {amount}, but only {headroom} of your capacity is free to set aside. Settling what you owe frees it sooner.

community.badKey: The public key must be 64 hex characters.
community.intro: Capacity is what the community has put behind each of them — it is earned by carrying a debt and paying it, so it starts at zero for everybody and nobody can grant it directly.
community.priceNote: The community scores them from what it has put behind them and what they owe. Move this to the right if you think worse of them than that, to the left if better. It changes only what your own wallet decides for you.
community.rotateBody: It must have been created there with a fresh recovery phrase. If the guardian threshold is above one, the other guardians will find this in their Requests inbox to co-sign. The rotation waits out the veto window before it can be finalized.
community.truncated: This node sent {shown} of {total} members. Somebody missing from this list may still be on the ledger — look them up by their address.
community.priceSummary: Your own reading of this member, kept on this device.
community.rotateSummary: Paste the public key from their NEW device.

contracts.extendAsked: The other party asks to extend this to {date} — sign or decline it under Requests.
contracts.extendWaiting: An extension to {date} is waiting for the other party's signature — track or withdraw it under Requests.
contracts.insuredTitle: The community stands behind this: it reserved capacity when it was accepted, and if it defaults the underwriters whose backing carried it become your debtors instead.
contracts.sealedTitle: Rounded up to conceal the exact figure — not the precise amount.
contracts.uninsuredTitle: Nobody but the creditor is behind this one. It reserved no capacity and triggers no community recourse if it defaults — which is how trade with someone new normally begins.

errors.ET-ADM-002: One of the keys is already registered to a member.
errors.ET-ADM-003: That key list is not usable: it is empty, or longer than one account may hold.
errors.ET-ARB-001: This contract has no arbitration terms.
errors.ET-ARB-002: You are not on this contract's panel.
errors.ET-ARB-007: The attestation window is still open — the award is decided when it closes.
errors.ET-BND-001: You have reached your activity limit for now. Each action sets aside a little of your available capacity, and it comes back to you shortly — nothing is charged and no one receives it. Settling what you owe frees capacity sooner.
errors.ET-BND-002: This member's activity has not been exhausted for long enough to forfeit.
errors.ET-BND-003: This member has no set-aside activity to forfeit.
errors.ET-BND-004: There is nobody to carry this write yet. A trade is recorded by whoever has standing in the community: ask the member you are trading with to record it from their app, and it will create your account along with it.
errors.ET-BND-005: Your account is not active, so it carries no activity budget of its own — nothing has been set aside, and waiting will not release any. A member acting with you can still record this on your behalf. What stays open to you is winding down: settling, curing, handing on what you owe, and leaving.
errors.ET-BND-006: You have brought in as many people as your standing carries. Bringing somebody in holds a small part of what backs you for as long as their account exists, and unlike your activity allowance it does not come back at the next epoch. More backing on you opens more.
errors.ET-CAS-004: That member is not in your listing.
errors.ET-CTR-002: The contract is not in a state that allows this.
errors.ET-CTR-005: The maturity is shorter than the community minimum.
errors.ET-CTR-006: The contract is not due yet.
errors.ET-CTR-008: That maturity is further out than the community allows.
errors.ET-GOV-001: Your standing is not yet established enough to propose.
errors.ET-GOV-003: The value is outside the constitutional safe range.
errors.ET-GOV-004: This parameter is in its cooldown period.
errors.ET-GOV-007: Only underwriters seated by a ceremony vote: your backing came from inside the community, so it carries no assent.
errors.ET-GOV-008: You have already assented to this proposal.
errors.ET-MEM-003: A required signature is missing — that member must sign from a device holding their key.
errors.ET-MEM-004: You are suspended, so you may pay down what you owe but not take on new credit. This sale goes beyond what it settles between you.
errors.ET-ROT-001: No guardians are registered for this member.
errors.ET-ROT-002: Not enough guardian signatures for the threshold.
errors.ET-ROT-004: The veto window is still open.
errors.ET-ROT-006: That veto window is too short: it is the time you would have to refuse a recovery you did not ask for.
errors.ET-SED-001: The community has already endorsed as much new backing as one epoch allows. Try again after the boundary.
errors.ET-SED-002: This amendment seats you, so it is not yours to assent to.
errors.ET-TX-001: This transaction was already submitted. Compose it again to get a fresh one.
errors.ET-TX-002: This transaction's validity window has passed. Compose it again.
errors.ET-TX-003: That validity window is longer than the ledger accepts.
errors.ET-TX-004: The node could not read this transaction's envelope.
errors.ET-UWR-001: A declared supply cannot be raised. It is a promise from outside the community, so it is seated by a ceremony — the founding genesis, or a seed amendment the community endorses — and never by standing the community itself conferred. You may lower yours here.
errors.ET-UWR-002: Credit still stands on this supply. You may lower it only to what is currently drawn through you.
errors.ET-UWR-003: You are still an underwriter. Withdraw your supply before leaving.
errors.ET-VAL-001: That member is not eligible as a validator.
errors.ET-VAL-002: That would leave the community without enough validators to order anything.
errors.ET-VAL-003: That voting power is beyond what a single validator may hold.
errors.ET-VAL-004: That member has not registered the key their validator would sign with. Register one first — it is separate from the key that signs your obligations.
errors.ET-VAL-005: That key is already in use. A validator key belongs to one operator, and it can never be a key that signs obligations.
errors.signingChain: This node claims to be a different network than the one you chose. Nothing was signed.
errors.signingMismatch: This request does not match what the node asked you to sign. Nothing was signed.
errors.signingUndeclared: This network has no declared chain id, so this device will not sign for it. Enter it beside the node address in the network settings.
errors.signingLocked: Your vault is locked. Enter your passphrase to sign.
errors.signingCustody: This device could not reach its secure key store, so your keys are protected only by this app’s own storage. Review that in Backup & security before signing.

governance.intro: Constitutional changes happen by proposal and assent, and the vote belongs to the backing brought from outside the community. Every governed constant lives inside a hard safe range.

kind.seedAmendment: Seat {member} as an underwriter for {amount} brought from outside

governance.noMandate: Assent belongs to the underwriters a ceremony seated: the vote is a share of the backing brought from outside the community. Yours came from inside it, so you may propose, and this is not yours to sign.
governance.ownAmendment: This amendment seats you, so it is not yours to assent to — it would be a vote cast with the very backing it grants.
governance.redenomNote: Prices, debts, stakes and history all move together; relative positions are untouched.
governance.seedNote: The backing you bring comes from outside the community: if the members your standing reaches fail, this much of the loss becomes a debt you owe in goods and services. Nobody can propose this on your behalf, and you do not vote on your own.
governance.redenomSummary: Re-denomination rescales every amount on the ledger atomically.
governance.seedSummary: You are asking to be seated as an underwriter. It is a liability, not a rank.
governance.summary: Changes enact when underwriters holding {threshold} of the {seed} external seed concur.

myContracts.cureHint: To cure this default, sell to your creditor — their purchase discharges it and restores your capacity.
myContracts.extendPastHorizon: Extending past it keeps the debt and drops the insurance: nothing stays reserved, and your creditor bears it alone from then on. Your creditor signs this too.
myContracts.extendPastHorizonSummary: After {date} the community stops standing behind this debt.
myContracts.extendPreview: Ends {left} epochs from now, {added} later than it does today. Your creditor must sign this too; the due date above changes once they have.
myContracts.handOverCarries: What they take on is the whole of it: if it goes unpaid the default is recorded against them, not you, and the capacity it holds is theirs to lose.
myContracts.handOverDeadline: Handing it on is open until {date}, and closes when it matures — after that only a cure your creditor also signs will clear it.
myContracts.handOverHint: They must agree, and so must your creditor unless the community can back them for it — the claim moves, so it is theirs to consent to.
myContracts.handOverSummary: Somebody else takes this debt over.
myContracts.intro: When your creditor buys from you, the mutual debt settles by itself — and any other sale clears your debts oldest-first. Nothing to file; if you need more time, extend the maturity together with your creditor.
myContracts.summary: Debts you owe. You pay them back by selling.
myContracts.paybackHint: Sell to your creditor and this settles by itself; any other sale clears it oldest-first.

myWallet.backersHelp: Members who have put standing behind you, by carrying and being repaid. Standing is evidence of having owed and paid — it cannot be bought, and selling earns none of it.
myWallet.newcomersHelp: How many more people your standing carries into the ledger. Bringing somebody in holds a small part of what backs you for as long as their account exists — it is not a fee, nobody receives it, and unlike your activity allowance it does not come back at the next epoch. More backing on you opens more.
myWallet.bondAllowanceHelp: Free actions left this epoch. Beyond them, each action sets aside a small part of what you have to lose and gives it back a short while later — the ledger charges no fees, so it is never spent and nobody receives it. Currently set aside: {reserved}. The allowance comes with standing, so it is zero while nobody is backing you. Settling, curing, transferring and leaving are always free.
myWallet.bondForfeitNote: Amounts set aside this long can be forfeited by anyone — they stop coming back to you. Slow down, or settle debt to free capacity.
myWallet.bondSpentNote: Further actions set aside a small part of what you have to lose until the next epoch — it comes back to you, and nobody receives it. Settling, curing and leaving stay free regardless.
myWallet.bootstrapEligible: Nobody is backing you right now. That is where everybody starts, and where standing goes if trade does not renew it — it is not a refusal. Trade anyway: your obligations are uninsured until somebody carries one, and paying one back is what makes the community stand behind you. Until then your free actions come with the counterparty, so somebody with standing has to be on the trade. The one exception is the action your seat paid for: you can nominate guardians once on your own.
myWallet.capacityHelp: How much debt the community will stand behind for you. It is already net of the credit standing on you, so it is the ceiling on your next insured purchase. You may still buy beyond it — that part is simply not covered.
myWallet.conferrable: You may back others up to
myWallet.conferrableHelp: What you may put behind somebody else. It costs you nothing and it is not a balance you spend — back twenty people and your own capacity is unchanged. Only credit actually outstanding is bounded.
myWallet.debtHelp: Your outstanding debt across all contracts. It clears when you sell (your buyer takes it over), when you settle directly, or when a supporter's sale drains into it.
myWallet.noActor: A wallet needs a key. This device holds none yet — look around, and set one up when you want to trade.
myWallet.openDefaultHelp: Defaulted amount not yet cured. A default does not hand back the backing it drew, so your standing stays consumed until you cure it.
myWallet.openDefaultNote: The backing it drew stays consumed until you cure it, and your free actions are held until then — sell to your creditor; their purchase discharges it.
myWallet.qrHint: Selling? Have the buyer scan your address.
myWallet.ruleOff: Acceptance rule off: every incoming request waits for your signature.
myWallet.ruleOn: Acceptance rule: purchases scoring at or below {accept}% risk are signed for you, at or above {reject}% declined, the rest held for your review.
myWallet.unknownMember: This member does not exist on the ledger (anymore).
myWallet.bondSpentSummary: You have used every free action for this epoch.
myWallet.bondForfeitSummary: Your activity allowance has been fully used for {epochs} epochs running.
myWallet.openDefaultSummary: You have an open default of {amount}.

offers.intro: Their purchase arrives here when they scanned your QR, or as a code they show you. It is already signed; your signature creates their account and books the debt at once.
offers.openLineSent: Buying {amount} from {seller} — sent to their app, valid until {date}
offers.badCode: That is not a buyer’s code.
offers.chain: This code was signed for a different network.
offers.signature: The signature on this code does not match what it says. Nothing was signed.
offers.notForMe: This code names a different seller.
offers.expired: This code has expired. Ask the buyer for a new one.
offers.member: They are a member already, so this books the debt like any other purchase.
offers.newAccount: It holds one of the newcomers you can bring in for as long as that account exists. Nobody has backed them yet, so nothing binds them but the arbitration they named, if any.
offers.openIntro: One sent to their app needs nothing more; show the code only if they cannot see it. Once they sign, the trade appears in your history.
offers.forgetNote: A seller who already has the code can complete it until it expires.
offers.forgetSummary: Forgetting removes it from this device only.
offers.introSummary: Somebody with no account yet is buying from you.
offers.newAccountSummary: This trade creates their account, and if they do not pay the debt is yours alone.
offers.openSummary: Purchases you signed that wait for the seller.

network.devNote: Dev cluster consensus is the crash-fault protocol; Byzantine safety is the production engine's job and is verified in the node's BFT suite.
network.epochHelp: The ledger clock: maturities, decay, and network recomputations tick per epoch. One epoch is one day.
network.heightHelp: Committed blocks. Every block is an agreed, ordered batch of transactions.
network.insuredHelp: What the community is actually standing behind right now: the backing drawn through its underwriters. Declared supply is an upper bound and not this.
network.intro: Every node commits the same blocks and must land on bit-identical state. The state commitment below is that fingerprint.
network.membersHelp: Active members / all members ever admitted.
network.mempoolHelp: Queued transactions waiting for the next block.
network.noValidators: No validator set is registered on this dev ledger — the dev cluster commits by node quorum.
network.seedHelp: Backing brought from outside the community — at founding, or by a later ceremony. It is the only thing that grows what the community can really carry, and it is what governance votes with.
network.single: A second node is what makes a disagreement visible.
network.uninsuredHelp: Live obligations the community does not stand behind, borne by their creditors alone. A rising count means the seed is small, where the ceiling only tells you it is full.
network.utilisationHelp: How much of the community's insurable backing is already committed. At 100% new obligations are still allowed, but they are uninsured — nobody throttles them.
network.singleSummary: This network declares one node, so its answers are checked against nothing.
network.summary: Your community ledger is replicated by its charter validators.

actorChoice.body: edet is a community ledger: everyone holds their own key, and nobody is admitted by anybody. Create an identity and trade with a member — that trade is what puts you on the ledger — or restore an identity from its recovery phrase.
actorChoice.title: Who are you in this community?

economicsIntro.guardianCtaBody: Nominate guardians early (Settings → Account & recovery): trusted members who can jointly rotate your membership to a new key if this device is ever lost. A rotation waits out a veto window during which your current key can block a theft. Guardians can only be nominated while you still control your key.
economicsIntro.guardianCtaTitle: Set up account recovery before you need it
economicsIntro.intro: edet has no coins to spend — every transaction is a promise between two members, recorded on your community ledger. Here is what that means for you.
economicsIntro.point1Body: When you buy from someone, you don't hand over money — you take on a debt to them for the amount.
economicsIntro.point2Body: You clear your debt by selling onward to others. A sale first discharges what you owe — through your support circle too — and only the remainder becomes new debt for the buyer.
economicsIntro.point3Body: Every contract has a maturity (at least {epochs} epochs). If a debt isn't cleared by then, it can be marked as a default: your capacity drops sharply and anyone who staked on you is exposed. A late payment ("cure") repairs it.
economicsIntro.point4Body: How much you can owe is not a bank limit and not a score: it is the backing the community has actually staked on you, and it grows as you settle what you owe. Nobody grants it, and you cannot raise it alone. A brand-new community starts with everyone at zero — the first trades are simply not covered by anybody, and settling them is what creates the backing for the next ones.
economicsIntro.title: How buying and selling works

identity.awaiting: Waiting for a member to trade with you…
identity.confirmBody: To make sure it is written down: what is word number {n} of your phrase?
identity.confirmError: That's not the right word — check your written phrase.
identity.createDesc: Generates a 12-word recovery phrase; your first purchase from a member is what creates your account.
identity.offeredBody: A member has recorded a trade with your key. Signing it is what creates your account — read it first: it is an obligation, not a formality.
identity.phraseBody: This is your recovery phrase. Write it down and keep it offline — it is shown only once and never stored. Whoever holds it holds this identity; without it, a lost device means a lost key.
identity.restoreBody: Enter your 12-word recovery phrase. The key is re-derived locally — the phrase never leaves this device — and the ledger is asked which membership it belongs to.
identity.restoreDesc: Re-derives your key and finds your membership on the ledger.
identity.restoreInvalid: That is not a valid recovery phrase.
identity.restoreNotFound: No member on this ledger holds this key.
identity.shareBody: Your identity key is ready and safely in this device's vault. Nobody has to admit you: hand this key to a member you are trading with — they scan the QR or paste the key when they record the trade — and the trade itself puts you on the ledger. It will appear here for you to review and sign.

localeSetup.body: The rest of this wizard — including the tour — will be shown in the language you pick here. You can change these settings later under Settings.
localeSetup.title: Choose your language and formats

network.body: edet is not one ledger — it is a community that keeps one. Whatever you build here, the standing others put behind you and the record of what you settled, lives on the network you pick now and cannot be moved to another. Pick the one your community runs.
network.crosscheck: This network publishes {n} nodes. Your app asks all of them the same questions and shows you whether their answers agree — so no single node has to be taken at its word.
network.label: Network
network.single: This network publishes one node, so there is nothing to check its answers against. That is fine for a node you run yourself, and a reason to be careful with one you do not.

pendingWallet.awaiting: No trade yet. Record a purchase under Transactions, or have a buyer scan your key.
pendingWallet.body: Record it under Transactions: scanning the seller's QR sends it to their app, and a code you can show them is kept in case. Their signature seats you and books the debt at once. Selling first works too: the buyer scans this key and records the purchase, and it comes back here for your signature. An account that holds nothing for a year — no trade in it, nothing owed, nothing backing it — is retired, and your next trade seats a new one at the same address.
pendingWallet.buying: You are BUYING. Sign and you owe {amount}.
pendingWallet.capacityHelp: What the community will let you owe. Zero until somebody backs you, and settling what you owe is what earns it.
pendingWallet.debtHelp: Nothing yet — this key has never traded.
pendingWallet.offeredBody: Signing it is what creates your account — read it first: it is an obligation, not a formality.
pendingWallet.qrHint: Selling? Have the buyer scan this.
pendingWallet.selling: You are SELLING. Sign and they owe you {amount}.

receivables.intro: Marking a default protects the community by making the risk visible, and it unlocks the cure path and arbitration.
receivables.panelIntro: Both parties consented to the panel. Attest the amount you find justified; when the quorum concurs, the median (capped) mints for the creditor.

backup.backendKeychain: Device key held in the OS keychain — browser-storage dumps alone cannot open the vault.
backup.backendKeystore: Device key wrapped by the hardware-backed Android Keystore — app-storage dumps alone cannot open the vault.
backup.backendLocal: Device key in local app storage (wrapping only) — the desktop app uses the OS keychain; on Android the per-app sandbox isolates this storage.
backup.badFile: This is not a valid edet backup file.
backup.description: It also carries your local names, and nothing else — the ledger itself lives on your community's nodes, and your recovery phrase is never included. Identities created from a phrase are restorable from the phrase alone; the backup matters for seeds that have no phrase, like members you admitted or recovered here.
backup.imported: Backup restored — {count} identities imported into the vault.
backup.keyLossBody: That is the primary path back. Without the phrase (and without a backup of this vault), the key is gone; if you nominated guardians in advance, a threshold of them can rotate your membership to a new key after the veto window, keeping your standing and history. Without guardians, the only way back is to start again with a new key: your old standing stays with the lost key, and its open debts will default at maturity, falling on whoever was backing them.
backup.keyLossTitle: If your key is lost or stolen
backup.keyTheftBody: Act immediately: have your guardians request a rotation to a new key of yours (your old key would veto a thief's rotation — a thief's key can't stop your guardians), and warn your trading partners. Treat the phrase and backup files as equivalent to the key: guard all of them.
backup.noFile: Choose a backup file or paste its contents first.
backup.passTooShort: Use a passphrase of at least 8 characters.
backup.title: Backup & security
backup.vaultStatus: Identity vault: {count} seeds, encrypted at rest (XChaCha20-Poly1305, device-key wrapped).
backup.passphraseOn: A passphrase is set: this device asks for it before it will open the vault or sign anything.
backup.downgrade: This device could not reach its secure key store, so the key that encrypts your seeds is sitting in this app’s own storage beside them. Anything that can read the app’s data can open the vault.
backup.downgradeAdvice: Signing is blocked until you acknowledge this. A passphrase below restores a second factor; exporting a backup and restoring on a healthy device removes the problem.
backup.unreadable: This device cannot open the key it holds — it was restored or reset. Restore your identity from your recovery phrase.
backup.unreadableAdvice: Nothing is wrong with this phone’s key store. The key that protected your seeds stayed on the old device, and the copy that came across cannot be opened by anything. Your recovery phrase is the way back.
backup.passphraseChange: Change or remove the vault passphrase
backup.passphraseHelp: Your seeds cannot be read without it, by anyone, this app included. It is never stored and cannot be reset — your recovery phrase is the way back. Leave both fields empty to remove one.
backup.vaultPassMismatch: The two passphrases do not match.
backup.descriptionSummary: A backup file carries the identities held on this device, encrypted with a passphrase you choose.
backup.keyLossSummary: Lost: your recovery phrase re-derives your key on any device.
backup.keyTheftSummary: Stolen: there is no freeze — whoever holds the key or phrase IS this identity.
backup.passphraseSummary: A second factor beside this device.

Take it from whoever runs the network — it is in the genesis file and on the Network status of every node — never from the node you are about to trust: a node that names the chain chooses which ledger you sign for.

connection.chainDetail: Take it from whoever runs the network — it is in the genesis file and on the Network status of every node — never from the node you are about to trust: a node that names the chain chooses which ledger you sign for.

identity.nicknameNote: Names never leave this device — on the ledger you are your membership, not a username.
identity.phraseNote: The phrase is never stored anywhere — whoever holds it can become you, and without it a lost device cannot be recovered (unless your guardians rotate you to a new key). Keep it written down, offline.
identity.title: Identity
identity.phraseSummary: Your identity key derives from your recovery phrase.

recovery.current: Any {threshold} of these guardians can request a rotation; the veto window is {window} epochs.
recovery.description: They are trusted members you nominate in advance. A rotation waits out a veto window during which your current key can block a theft.
recovery.exitBody: You must carry no open default, no operation bond of yours still set aside, you must have withdrawn any supply you underwrite, and the community must still have enough validators without you. Your history stays on the ledger. A key that has exited cannot rejoin as itself; an account retired for standing empty can.
recovery.pendingBody: Opened {date}. If you did not ask your guardians for this, veto it now.
recovery.pendingTitle: A key rotation is pending for your account
recovery.title: Account & recovery
recovery.descriptionSummary: Guardians can jointly move your membership to a new key if this device is lost.
recovery.exitSummary: Voluntary exit is only valid once you owe nothing and hold nothing outstanding.

tour.description: Replay the introduction tour if you'd like a refresher.
tour.title: Tour

support.capNone: no route yet — settle a trade between you
support.intro: Your own share clears your debts (your buyer takes them over), the rest clears the debts of the people you list. Listing needs no consent; draining does: each beneficiary must approve you as a supporter.
support.reachClears: could clear up to {amount} of what you owe — standing you would have earned by paying it yourself
support.reachNothing: you owe nothing they could clear right now
support.reachUnknown: your obligations are not visible here
support.selfEarnsNothing: Your buyer takes them over, and only a debt you settle with the person you owe writes anything behind you.
support.supportersIntro: Their sales clear your debts oldest first, and nothing drains through until you approve. Approving is a real trade, not a formality. A debt cleared for you is discharged without earning you anything, while paying it yourself is the one act that builds your standing and with it your credit limit — so the choice is relief now against standing later, and it is yours alone. Approval is also not enough to make a route: an edge carries at most what the two of you have staked in each other, which is nothing until you have traded and settled.
support.weightsNote: Shares always total 100% — raising one lowers the others (waterfill). Your own share clears your debts partially, at the balance you choose; at 0% your sales support only your circle.
support.selfEarnsNothingSummary: Your own share clears your debts without earning you standing.
support.summary: Every sale you make is split by these shares.
support.supportersSummary: These members list you: their sales can clear your debts, once you approve them.
support.zeroShare: {member} is at 0% and would not be listed — raise their share, or remove the row.
support.supportersUnknown: Who lists you is not visible here — this node answered without your credential. Anyone supporting you is still waiting on your approval.
support.sharesUnknown: Your breakdown is not visible here — this node answered without your credential.

community.text: Every member of the ledger, and what the community has put behind each of them. Standing is not granted here and cannot be bought — it is the record of debts already carried and paid.
community.title: Your community

contracts.text: Contracts track your open debts and their maturity. They clear as you trade — sell to your creditor and the mutual debt settles by itself. The only thing left to file is a maturity extension.
contracts.title: Debts you owe

receivables.text: The mirror view: contracts where you are the creditor, with the actions a creditor has — including marking an overdue debt as defaulted.
receivables.title: Owed to you

settings.text: Language, theme, number formats, node connection, and account recovery (guardians). You can replay this tour from here at any time.
settings.title: Settings and recovery

support.text: Choose whose debts your sales help clear, and approve the supporters who list you. This is the cascade that makes selling clear debt.
support.title: Support circle

transactions.text: Record a purchase here. It first clears what the seller already owes — to you, then through their support circle — and only the remainder becomes your new debt.
transactions.title: Record a transaction

walletHeader.text: This is who you are on the community ledger: your avatar, your local display name, and your membership status.
walletHeader.title: Your identity

walletMetrics.text: These cards show what the community backs you for, what you owe, and who is backing you. Each card has a help icon with a plain-English explanation.
walletMetrics.title: Your standing at a glance

walletQr.text: Selling something? The buyer scans this QR (or types your address) to record the purchase — the debt they take from you IS the payment.
walletQr.title: Get paid

welcome.text: Let's take a quick look at your wallet, your community, and where to find settings.
welcome.title: Welcome to edet

transactions.arbToggle: Agree on an arbitration panel (optional, immutable after)
transactions.empty: Nothing yet — tap + to record your first purchase.
transactions.keyedExplainer: This purchase reaches the seller on their invitation, which their QR carries; without one it leaves this device as a code you show them. Either way their signature creates your account and books the debt at once.
transactions.keyedSummary: Buying is taking on a debt to the seller — and you have no account yet, so their signature creates one.
transactions.maturityDisclosure: The debtor's standing stays consumed, and where the community was standing behind the debt, the underwriters whose backing carried it become the creditor's debtors instead.
transactions.maturitySummary: Unpaid at its maturity, this can be marked a default by anyone. Today is {date}, epoch {epoch}.
transactions.offerBody: Your purchase is signed on this device. They scan the code, or you send them the text; they check it and sign, and their signature creates your account and books the debt at once. The code stays under Transactions until then.
transactions.offerSummary: Show this to the seller — their signature completes the purchase.
transactions.offerFallback: The seller's app could not take it through the node, so show them this code instead.
transactions.purchaseExplainer: Enter the seller's wallet address or scan their QR. The purchase binds once they sign it from their app, and if the seller has open debts your purchase automatically helps clear them.
transactions.purchaseSummary: Buying is taking on a debt to the seller — that is the payment.
transactions.sentToSeller: Sent to the seller — it shows under their Requests. The code stays under Transactions in case they cannot see it.
transactions.unbackedCounterparty: That is not a mark against them — every account starts there. If the amount matters to you, name an arbiter below: it is the only thing that binds somebody with no standing to an outcome.
transactions.unbackedSummary: Nobody has backed them yet, so nothing binds them to deliver.
transactions.uninsuredTheirs: Nothing is reserved, and if you do not pay, the seller bears it alone. They may still agree — that is their decision to make — but it is worth knowing you are asking for it.
transactions.uninsuredTheirsSummary: Not insured: this is more than your capacity carries.
transactions.beyondHorizonTheirs: Nothing is reserved, and if you do not pay, the seller bears it alone. A shorter term is insured; a longer one can be re-accepted when it falls due.
transactions.beyondHorizonTheirsSummary: Not insured: this maturity is past the {horizon} epochs the community stands behind a claim for.
transactions.truncated: This node sent {shown} of {total} trades on the ledger, so your history here may be incomplete.

txkind.accept: {debtor} takes on a debt of {amount} to {creditor} (maturity {maturity} epochs)
txkind.cure: Cure {amount} of the default on contract #{contract}
txkind.rotateRequest: Rotate {member}'s membership to a new key (guardian recovery)
txkind.rotateVeto: Veto the pending key rotation of {member}
txkind.sale: Sale of {amount} from {seller} to {buyer} (cascade discharge first)
txkind.transfer: Transfer contract #{contract} to {to} as new debtor

waiting.requestBody: A request needs your signature. Open edet to decide it.
waiting.supportBody: {count} waiting for your approval in your support circle. Open edet → Support Circle.

unlock.title: Unlock your identity
unlock.body: Your seeds are encrypted with this passphrase as well as with this device. Nobody can read them without it — this app included.
unlock.wrong: That passphrase does not open this vault.
unlock.forgotten: Forgotten it? There is no reset — that is what makes it worth having. Restore this identity from its recovery phrase on a fresh profile.
